target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where QQBot logout/setup credential cleanup could treat prototype-inherited named account entries or inherited credential fields as if they were explicit user config. In affected programmatic config shapes, logout could either report cleanup for config the user did not own or continue resolving an inherited account as configured after cleanup skipped the write.

## Why This Change Was Made

QQBot credential cleanup now uses own-property checks across the whole logout/setup account path, not only the low-level credential remover. Named account resolution, default-account selection, setup account updates, bridge account resolution, and credential clearing now agree that only own `channels.qqbot.accounts.<id>` entries and own `clientSecret` / `clientSecretFile` fields are mutable user config.

The latest follow-up also normalizes a named account object to its own enumerable properties before bridge credential resolution, so an own `accounts.<id>` object cannot inherit `clientSecret` or `clientSecretFile` from its prototype.

## User Impact

QQBot logout and setup cleanup now ignore prototype-inherited account data and only clear credentials that are actually present on the user's config object. Normal own account logout still removes `clientSecret` / `clientSecretFile`, keeps non-secret fields such as `appId`, and writes the cleaned config through the existing runtime path.

Exact head: `678828757e32286b1fb955989c84a0b54f7e594b`

The channel health monitor's retry logic previously bypassed the `maxRestartsPerHour` budget and skipped updating `lastRestartAt` for restarts classified as "continuing pending restarts". target.title: fix(acpx): drain leased descendants when turns are aborted
target.body:
Refs #104847

## Current Status

**Draft.** The current head is the single ACPX-focused commit `be52e466068dd57e0f1f8c24d4ab8dd5612e5405`, rebased onto upstream `main` at `477f3af6883af1176fe88e9f8c561d6769097715`. Public exact-head macOS process, control-plane, abort-feedback, startup fail-closed, launchd service proof, and full CI pass. The previous current-head review reported one blocking P1 because the broad startup reaper dropped survivor evidence; this head propagates that evidence and adds the requested pending-lease regression. The PR remains Draft pending a fresh current-head review and explicit maintainer acceptance of the fail-closed ACPX compatibility and availability contract.

## Problem

Cancelling an ACP-backed turn could stop the visible reply while leaving an ACPX-owned worker alive after it detached from the wrapper's PPID tree. The existing reaper validated a wrapper process and walked its current parent/child tree, but `setsid`, double-fork, or later reparenting could move the autonomous worker outside that tree. The fast-abort path could also log cleanup failure and still report normal abort success.

## Root Cause

OpenClaw owned the outer ACPX runtime lifecycle but did not persist a process-ownership identity that survived PPID changes. Cancellation also treated cooperative ACP protocol cancellation as the lifecycle boundary, even though protocol cancel does not guarantee that detached host processes are gone.

The startup path had a second correctness gap: broad wrapper-root orphan cleanup called the survivor-aware termination helper but discarded `survivingPids`. A pending lease with `rootPid <= 0` could therefore be marked closed and allow ACPX registration even while an owned orphan remained alive.

## Code Path

1. `/stop` reaches the ACP manager cancellation path through `src/auto-reply/reply/abort.ts`.
2. `src/acp/control-plane/manager.cancel-session.ts` evicts the cached runtime handle and starts `close()` before best-effort protocol cancellation, so a rejected or never-settling protocol cancel cannot gate containment.
3. `extensions/acpx/src/runtime.ts` closes the ACPX turn owner and drains its process lease.
4. `extensions/acpx/src/process-reaper.ts` combines the live PPID tree with random lease and Gateway-instance markers, sends TERM, refreshes inventory, revalidates process identity before KILL, and performs a final survivor check.
5. `extensions/acpx/src/service.ts` drains stale open or pending leases before backend registration and now treats broad-reaper survivors as a startup failure.
6. Abort feedback reports containment failure instead of claiming success when cleanup cannot be verified.

## Behavior Changes

- ACP cancellation starts close and lease drain before best-effort protocol cancellation.
- Reparented descendants remain attributable by inherited random lease ID and Gateway instance ID.
- POSIX inventory uses bounded `ps eww` output only for in-memory matching and never logs process environments.
- Windows uses `Win32_Process` PID, PPID, command, and executable inventory; PPID-tree descendants use exact command and parent identity for delayed escalation.
- TERM-resistant targets are escalated only after fresh identity revalidation. A disappeared or reused PID is not signaled as the original target.
- Every targeted PID is included in final liveness verification even when TERM or KILL throws.
- Startup refuses ACPX registration when an open or pending lease cannot be verified or drained, including survivors returned by broad wrapper-root cleanup.
- Generic persistent `exec` and `process` background sessions are outside the ACPX lease path and keep their existing lifecycle.

## Compatibility And Migration

- No stored schema, config key, or user-data migration is introduced. Existing lease records keep the same shape.
- Cancellation now closes and evicts the reusable live ACP runtime handle; a later turn must reopen or resume instead of reusing that handle.
- Startup availability changes intentionally: an unverifiable or undrainable stale ACPX lease blocks backend registration until containment succeeds or an operator resolves the stale process.
- There is no compatibility fallback in this patch. Maintainer acceptance of this fail-closed policy is required before Ready status.

## Evidence

### Before: launchd and process-group boundary

Public GitHub-hosted `macos-14` proof demonstrates that `launchctl bootout` removes the launchd leader and plain child while a `start_new_session` child and double-fork daemon survive:

- Run: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29187863352
- Baseline job: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29187863352/job/86637125671
- Artifact: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29187863352/artifacts/8258570570
- Artifact SHA-256: `b7a13f5f39f456ffc5070f427e522c1678098c71afd190b33d32e162e4d913b3`
- Evidence-only PR: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/pull/3

This is why launchd or process-group cleanup alone is not complete containment.

### After: exact-head candidate proof

Public GitHub-hosted `macos-14` proof checked out and verified `be52e466068dd57e0f1f8c24d4ab8dd5612e5405`:

- Run: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29187863352
- Candidate job: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29187863352/job/86637125683
- Artifact: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29187863352/artifacts/8258578919
- Artifact SHA-256: `4eb6a4389962505d62141adc0da2c326cef09426e3e7f5135cf80a1f939e4a72`
- ACPX process/runtime/service suites: 4 files, 104 tests passed.
- ACP manager cancellation: 1 file, 4 tests passed.
- Abort and operator feedback: 1 file, 33 tests passed.
- The new regressions prove broad startup survivor propagation and startup refusal for a `rootPid: 0` pending lease whose owned orphan remains alive.

### Service-managed ownership proof

The same exact-head job runs the production lease and reaper implementation under a launchd-managed service:

- Before abort: service alive, lease-owned reparented descendant alive, unrelated persistent background alive.
- After abort: service alive, lease-owned descendant gone, unrelated persistent background alive.
- Cleanup inspected and terminated the leased PID and reported no survivors.
- Every evidence pipeline uses `set -o pipefail`, so harness failure cannot be hidden by `tee`.

### Full CI

- Exact-head full CI: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29187865437
- Status: passed for exact head `be52e466068dd57e0f1f8c24d4ab8dd5612e5405`; all selected jobs completed successfully.
- Upstream PR checks: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104929/checks
- Local lightweight preflight: targeted `oxfmt` and `git diff --check` passed. Builds, type checks, lint, and test suites run in GitHub Actions.

## Tests Added Or Updated

- Real POSIX detached and reparented lease cleanup.
- Lease environment matching with Gateway-instance isolation.
- TERM-resistant escalation, signal failures, final survivor verification, and PID-reuse identity revalidation.
- Windows process inventory and delayed PPID-tree escalation identity.
- Broad startup reaper survivor propagation.
- Pending lease with `rootPid <= 0` blocks startup when an owned orphan survives.
- Runtime close failure marks containment lost and propagates failure.
- Cancellation starts close and lease drain before rejected or never-settling protocol cancel.
- `/stop` returns containment failure instead of false success.

## Performance

- Process inventory runs only during ACPX cancellation and startup stale-lease recovery, not on the steady-state turn path.
- POSIX process output is bounded to 8 MiB.
- Cleanup deduplicates target PIDs and reuses one broad-root result for pending leases sharing a wrapper root.

## Risk And Rollback

- The deliberate compatibility risk is loss of live-handle reuse after cancellation.
- The deliberate availability risk is startup refusal when stale ACPX containment cannot be proven.
- Process ownership matching is security-sensitive; PID reuse is handled by fresh identity checks before escalation and by final inventory verification.
- Reverting the commit restores cooperative cancel reuse, PPID-only cleanup, and the previous startup behavior.

## Maintainer Decision Required

Should OpenClaw intentionally override upstream ACPX cooperative-cancel semantics by closing and evicting the reusable runtime handle, and should any unverifiable or undrainable stale ACPX lease block backend startup?

Recommended policy: accept the fail-closed contract because the alternative can report a turn stopped while an autonomous credentialed worker remains alive. This PR will stay Draft until the relevant ACPX/runtime owner explicitly accepts that compatibility and availability tradeoff.

## Not Tested

- No private Claude credentials or paid-provider runtime were used.
- Public CI uses deterministic real host processes plus the production ACPX lease, reaper, control-plane, and abort-feedback implementations.

target.title: fix(memory-wiki): honor memory_search deadline during wiki exhaustive scan
target.body:
Closes #104719

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running `memory_search` with `corpus="wiki"` or `corpus="all"` against a large compiled-wiki vault would hit `memory_search timed out after 15s` when digest-selected candidates underfilled `maxResults`. The wiki supplement then continued a full remaining-vault Markdown scan after the tool had already timed out, so agents lost wiki recall and the host kept doing orphan I/O.

## Why This Change Was Made

The memory tool already owns a fixed deadline (`AbortSignal`), but the corpus-supplement bridge never forwarded it into memory-wiki search. Exhaustive underfill scanning then read remaining pages with no cancellation points.

This PR threads an optional `signal` through `MemoryCorpusSupplement.search` → wiki corpus supplement → `searchMemoryWiki` / `searchWikiCorpus`, and makes page reads batch-aware so an aborted deadline returns partial results and stops further file I/O.

Unlike approaches that permanently disable exhaustive backfill for supplements (which need a feature-owner completeness tradeoff), exhaustive recall remains the default when the search is still within budget. Direct `wiki_search` is unchanged except that it can also honor an optional signal if a caller provides one.

## User Impact

Agents using compiled-wiki supplements through `memory_search` no longer leave large orphan vault scans running after a tool timeout. On-budget multi-result wiki recall still gets exhaustive underfill when needed. Operators avoid multi-second post-timeout host work on large vaults.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (agent review follow-up)

Lint (exact CS finding):
- Fixed `oxc(no-map-spread)` at `extensions/memory-wiki/src/query.ts` page-read map:
  `{ ...summary, raw }` → `Object.assign({}, summary, { raw })` (same shape, no map spread).
- Focused oxlint on the file: `Found 0 warnings and 0 errors` on `extensions/memory-wiki/src/query.ts`.

Focused tests (all pass after fix):

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-wiki/src/query.test.ts -t "104719"
# Test Files  1 passed (1)
# Tests  4 passed | 41 skipped (45)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  extensions/memory-wiki/src/corpus-supplement.test.ts \
  extensions/memory-core/src/tools.citations.test.ts
# Test Files  2 passed (2)
# Tests  30 passed (30)
```

`git diff --check` clean on touched files. Head: `e3a005d3b`.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: (1) exact-head lint blocker on abort-aware page map; (2) memory-wiki exhaustive underfill ignored the memory_search deadline so host work could continue after tool timeout.
- Environment: local macOS arm64, openclaw checkout at `e3a005d3b`, Node via repo Vitest harness (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`).
- Current-main contrast: `searchMemoryCorpusSupplements` did not accept/forward an AbortSignal; `searchWikiCorpus` underfill listed and read every remaining Markdown path with no abort checks (`extensions/memory-wiki/src/query.ts` exhaustive path). Page-read map used object spread rejected by `oxc(no-map-spread)`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. `npx oxlint --config .oxlintrc.json extensions/memory-wiki/src/query.ts` → 0 errors
  2. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-wiki/src/query.test.ts -t "104719"`
  3. Representative-vault abort I/O proof (new test): 80-page vault; abort after first 16-file batch; assert partial pages returned and `mdReads < padCount` (further batches never start)
  4. On-budget exhaustive still finds body-only needle when signal not aborted
  5. memory_search tool tests assert deadline `AbortSignal` forwarded into supplements
- Evidence after fix (redacted transcript):
  ```text
  ✓ returns no wiki hits when the caller deadline is already aborted (#104719)
  ✓ still exhaustively finds body-only hits when the deadline is not aborted (#104719)
  ✓ stops mid-scan when the deadline aborts during exhaustive page reads (#104719)
  ✓ returns partial pages and stops further batch reads after abort (#104719)
     (80-page representative vault; abort trips at batch boundary; partial < full vault)
  ✓ forwards effective agent context to memory_search corpus=wiki supplements
     (expects signal: AbortSignal)
  ✓ forwards effective agent context to memory_search corpus=all supplements
     (expects signal: AbortSignal)
  oxlint query.ts: Found 0 warnings and 0 errors
  ```
- Control check: on-budget exhaustive underfill still finds a body-only page outside digest candidates. Pre-aborted search returns `[]` without scanning. Mid-scan abort returns partial pages and does not complete the remaining vault batches (instrumented `fs.readFile` count on sources).
- Observed result after fix: deadline-aborted wiki search stops/returns partial without full remaining-vault I/O; non-aborted search retains complete exhaustive underfill; memory_search passes `deadlineSignal` into supplements; exact-head no-map-spread lint clean.
- What was not tested: live 77 MB / 1,220-file vault timing on a real Gateway (issue’s large-vault numbers); permanent digest-only supplement mode (intentionally not chosen — preserves completeness when within budget).


## Linked PR context

Open PR #104793 targets the same issue with deadline propagation **plus** `exhaustiveFallback: false` for supplements. ClawSweeper on that PR asked for feature-owner approval of digest-only completeness tradeoff and stronger query-level tests. This PR follows the safer half of that guidance: signal propagation + abort-aware I/O without changing on-budget recall completeness.

## AI disclosure

This fix was authored with AI assistance (Grok / xAI contributor agent). Human operator requested an automated find→fix→PR pipeline; proof is local Vitest transcripts above.

target.title: fix(scripts/pr): refuse GraphQL prepare push when rebases rewrite ancestry
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`scripts/pr` `prepare-sync-head` defaulted to GitHub GraphQL `createCommitOnBranch`. That mutation can only layer a tree delta onto `expectedHeadOid` — it **cannot move a commit's parent**. After a rebase onto newer `main`, it applied the intended tree on top of the *stale* PR tip parent. Tree verification passed, but the GitHub three-dot diff (`base...head`) then pulled in unrelated mainline files (real incident: a focused 4-file +25/-9 PR rendered as 54 files, +3078/-419).

Closes #103358.

## Fix

- Detect when the prepared head rewrites ancestry relative to the lease SHA (`prep_push_ancestry_must_move`): true after a rebase, false for pure fast-forward/descendant tips.
- For **same-repository** rebased tips, push with `git push --force-with-lease` so ancestry moves with the tree.
- **Fail closed** (exit 2, with #103358 guidance) when a **cross-repository** tip needs an ancestry rewrite but only the GraphQL write is available — GraphQL there would silently re-pollute the diff.
- Keep the GraphQL `createCommitOnBranch` path for non-ancestry (fast-forward-style) fork updates, so signed web commits are preserved where they are correct.
- Verify parent OIDs after push (not only tree equality), and persist `PR_IS_CROSS_REPOSITORY` in `pr-meta`.

## Evidence — live behavior proof

Ran a real reproduction against actual local git repos (a bare "remote" + clone), sourcing the **shipped** `prep_push_ancestry_must_move` from `scripts/pr-lib/push.sh` (no mocks). It reconstructs the exact `createCommitOnBranch` object with `git commit-tree -p <lease_sha>`, then compares the GitHub-style three-dot diff (`merge-base(main,head)...head`) for both paths:

```
== 4. DETECTOR: does ancestry have to move? ==
RESULT: ancestry_must_move = TRUE  (rebase rewrote parent -> git force-with-lease required)

== 5a. BUGGY PATH: GraphQL layers tree on the STALE lease parent ==
graphql-style commit: 7b3af1e (parent=010189d  <- stale PR tip)
--- three-dot diff (base...graphql) file count:
    feature.txt
    main1.txt
    main2.txt
    main3.txt
    => 4 files (POLLUTED: pulls in unrelated main1/2/3.txt)

== 5b. FIXED PATH: force-with-lease moves ancestry ==
remote pr-branch now at: 8b86d47 (== prepared head: YES)
--- three-dot diff (base...pushed) file count:
    feature.txt
    => 1 file (CLEAN: only the intended change)

== 6. fast-forward tip is NOT flagged (GraphQL path preserved) ==
RESULT: fast-forward tip ancestry_must_move = FALSE ✔

==================== SUMMARY ====================
GraphQL/stale-parent three-dot diff : 4 files (polluted)
force-with-lease three-dot diff     : 1 file  (focused)
detector rebase=TRUE, fast-forward=FALSE : correct
```

This demonstrates the end-to-end behavior on a real remote: the old GraphQL path yields the polluted 4-file three-dot diff, the leased rewrite yields the clean 1-file diff, and fast-forward tips are correctly left on the GraphQL path.

## Verification (regression tests)

- `test/scripts/pr-prepare-gates.test.ts` (+137): ancestry detector truth table (rebase vs. pure-descendant) and the mode-selection branch (same-repo → force-with-lease; cross-repo ancestry rewrite → refuse GraphQL, exit 2).
- Did NOT change the GraphQL path for non-ancestry fork updates.

## Security

No change to repository permissions, secrets, dependency execution, or untrusted-file handling. Retains exact-SHA `--force-with-lease` and shell-escaped persisted metadata.

target.title: fix(slack): log native progress stream start failures instead of silently swallowing

## What Problem This Solves

When native Slack progress streaming starts, overlapping progress callbacks can await the same in-flight `startSlackStream` promise. The **initiating** `updateNativeProgressStream()` path already reports failures via `runtime.error`, but the prior PR added a second `logVerbose` in the waiter catch — duplicating diagnostics for one rejection.

## Changes

- **Remove duplicate waiter logging** — `waitForNativeProgressStreamStart()` keeps a silent catch that only marks `streamFailed` and returns `false`.
- **Improve single-owner diagnostic** — initiating `updateNativeProgressStream()` now reports `start` vs `update` phase in the existing `runtime.error` message.
- **Add production-equivalent overlap regression** — uses the real `createChannelProgressDraftGate` with staggered overlapping progress callbacks; asserts exactly **one** `runtime.error` and **no** waiter `logVerbose` duplicate.

## Evidence

**Current head:** `94aad230`

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway terminal scrollback (`TerminalOutputRing`) keeps a UTF-16 code-unit capped buffer for attach replay and `terminal.text`. When a single PTY write is at least as large as the configured scrollback cap, the ring retained the tail with raw `chunk.slice(chunk.length - cap)`. If an emoji or other non-BMP character sits across that cut, the snapshot/replay/text payload can start with a lone low surrogate (often rendered as U+FFFD).

This is the same class of bug as worker SSH tunnel stderr tails (`#104621`) and worker bootstrap UTF-16 truncation (`#104619`), on the Control UI / Gateway terminal path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse `sliceUtf16Safe` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice` for the oversized-chunk retention path only. Multi-chunk eviction still drops whole PTY write chunks and is unchanged. Cap semantics stay “UTF-16 code units”; after a safe slice the stored `total` matches the kept string length so the ring cannot overshoot when the leading surrogate is dropped.

target.title: fix(moonshot): forward abort signal through Kimi web search provider
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users cancelling an agent run while a Kimi (Moonshot) `web_search` request was pending would leave that HTTP request running. The parent execution signal reached the generic web-search runtime, but the Kimi provider discarded the execution context, so the request could remain open and eventually resolve after cancellation.

The Kimi tool accepted only `args` and dropped the tool execution context — `executeKimiWebSearchProviderTool` had no `opts` parameter and `createTool` ignored `context`. The downstream `runKimiSearch` already accepted a `signal` field but the caller never passed one in, so the signal died at the provider boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is a root-cause fix across the existing cancellation boundaries: the Kimi tool now accepts the execution context and passes its `AbortSignal` through `executeKimiWebSearchProviderTool` → `runKimiSearch` → `withTrustedWebSearchEndpoint` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` → `fetch()`.

The change does not alter Kimi configuration, schemas, cache keys, timeouts, SSRF policy, or response formatting. Regression coverage locks the signal handoff and proves that reverting the fix causes test failure.

## User Impact

Cancelling a run now promptly cancels an in-flight Kimi web search instead of consuming network and server resources until the configured timeout or response. Normal completed searches and cached results are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Signal path — full chain (source verified)

| Layer | File | Line | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tool entry | `kimi-web-search-provider.ts` | 63 | `execute: async (args, context)` accepts context |
| Signal pass | `kimi-web-search-provider.ts` | 66 | `{ signal: context?.signal }` |
| Tool exec | `kimi-web-search-provider.runtime.ts` | 349 | `opts?: { signal?: AbortSignal }` |
| Run search | `kimi-web-search-provider.runtime.ts` | 401 | `signal: opts?.signal` |
| Search client | `kimi-web-search-provider.runtime.ts` | 234 | `withTrustedWebSearchEndpoint({ signal: params.signal })` |
| SSRF guard | `provider-web-search.ts` | — | `fetchWithSsrFGuard({ signal })` |
| Timeout | `provider-web-search.ts` | — | `buildTimeoutAbortSignal({ signal })` |
| Native | `fetch()` | — | Native `AbortSignal` support |

### Real behavior proof — pre-aborted signal through full provider chain

```
[proof] Pre-aborted signal propagated through Kimi provider in 1293ms
[proof] error: Error: proof: pre-aborted signal
```

- Signal flows from provider.execute() through all intermediate layers to fetch()
- buildTimeoutAbortSignal sees pre-aborted parent signal → immediately aborts controller
- No network I/O occurs (fake API key passes the credential check)
- false-positive regression guard: if execute resolves (signal forwarding reverted) → test fails

  "errorType": "DOMException",
  "errorMessage": "proof: in-flight cancellation",

target.title: fix(gateway): bound base64url payload decode in agent runtime identity token
target.body:
## Summary

- **Problem:** `verifyAgentRuntimeIdentityToken` decodes the payload segment via `Buffer.from(value, "base64url")` inside `decodePayload` before HMAC signature verification. An attacker-provided token with a multi-megabyte payload segment triggers large Buffer allocation before the signature check can reject it.
- **Solution:** Added `MAX_BASE64URL_PAYLOAD_LENGTH = 4096` and reject oversized `payloadPart` before `decodePayload` is called. Every real caller produces a payloadPart of ~200 base64url characters, so 4096 is a generous safety margin and cannot affect legitimate use. The existing try/catch in decodePayload already returns undefined on malformed input, so the new early return is absorbed as a token validation failure rather than a crash.
- **What changed:** `src/gateway/agent-runtime-identity-token.ts` — `verifyAgentRuntimeIdentityToken` now rejects payloadPart longer than the bound.
- **What did NOT change:** Valid token decoding behavior; the error-handling contract (invalid tokens already return `undefined`).

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Unbounded base64url decode could allocate arbitrary memory on attacker-influenced input before HMAC verification; it is now bounded at 4096 characters.
- **Real environment tested:** Direct node function call against the patched module using `npx tsx`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  - `pnpm test src/gateway/agent-runtime-identity-token.test.ts` — 16/16 tests pass
  - Manual verification script:
    - Valid 132-char token → decoded (agentId=main, sessionKey=session-1) OK
    - Oversized 5000-char payload → rejected (returns undefined)
    - Boundary 4096-char payload = MAX → rejected
    - Valid-size (100-char) invalid base64 payload → returns undefined via decode fallback
    - null/undefined tokens → returns undefined

## Evidence

```text
Test 1 - 正常 token (132 chars): PASS
Test 2 - 超大 payload (5000 chars): PASS (rejected)
Test 3 - 边界 payload (4096 chars = MAX): PASS (rejected)
Test 4 - 小 payload (100 chars, 无效 base64): PASS (returns undefined via decode fallback)
Test 5 - null token: PASS
Test 6 - undefined token: PASS
```

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** `decodePayload` performed no input-length bound before `Buffer.from`, allowing unbounded allocation on malformed or abusive input.
- **Missing detection / guardrail:** No maximum-input-length check on the payload entry point before HMAC verification.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Coverage level:** Unit test
- **Target test file:** `src/gateway/agent-runtime-identity-token.test.ts`
- **Scenario to lock in:** A token whose payloadPart exceeds 4096 characters returns undefined; a normal-length token round-trips correctly.

_Follows the same pattern as the ed25519 base64url length guard in `src/infra/ed25519-signature.ts` (PR #104921)._

target.title: fix(parallel): reject invalid search counts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users selecting Parallel web search providers could pass malformed or out-of-range `count` values and still have the provider request proceed after local coercion or clamping.

## Why This Change Was Made

The paid Parallel REST provider and the free Parallel Search MCP provider now use the same strict positive-integer count validation at their tool boundary before building provider requests. This keeps the existing default/configured `maxResults` fallback and final 1-40 normalization while rejecting caller-supplied `count` values that do not match the advertised schema.

## User Impact

Parallel web search calls now fail fast with a clear count validation error for fractional, malformed string, or over-limit result counts instead of silently sending a different `max_results` value upstream.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: paid `parallel` and free `parallel-free` web search tools reject fractional, malformed-string, and over-limit `count` values before provider transport, while valid/default count behavior still works.
- Current-head focused tests at `b53c3f96fc19bc9cff42385944b126ae3bce5e82`: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/parallel/src/parallel-web-search-provider.test.ts extensions/parallel/src/parallel-free-web-search-provider.test.ts` passed with 2 files and 36 tests.
- Current-head real provider proof at `b53c3f96fc19bc9cff42385944b126ae3bce5e82`: `node --import tsx --input-type=module` ran the actual `parallel-free` provider tool from this checkout with `cacheTtlMinutes: 0` against Parallel's hosted keyless MCP.
- Real provider transcript:

```json
{
  "provider": "parallel-free",
  "invalid": [
    {
      "count": 4.5,
      "ok": true,
      "error": "count must be an integer from 1 to 40."
    },
    {
      "count": "3abc",
      "ok": true,
      "error": "count must be an integer from 1 to 40."
    },
    {
      "count": 41,
      "ok": true,
      "error": "count must be an integer from 1 to 40."
    }
  ],
  "valid": {
    "provider": "parallel-free",
    "count": 1,
    "resultCount": 1,
    "firstUrlHost": "github.com",
    "hasSessionId": true,
    "cached": false
  },
  "omitted": {
    "provider": "parallel-free",
    "count": 5,
    "resultCount": 5,
    "firstUrlHost": "docs.openclaw.ai",
    "hasSessionId": true,
    "cached": false
  }
}
```

- Targeted format: `node_modules\.bin\oxfmt.CMD --check --threads=1 extensions\parallel\src\parallel-web-search-provider.runtime.ts extensions\parallel\src\parallel-free-web-search-provider.runtime.ts extensions\parallel\src\parallel-web-search-provider.test.ts extensions\parallel\src\parallel-free-web-search-provider.test.ts` passed.
- Branch diff hygiene: `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` passed.
- Review proof: `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode branch --base upstream/main --engine codex --codex-bin <pixel relay wrapper>` passed with no accepted/actionable findings.
- Duplicate search: open PR and issue searches for `parallel count max_results web_search` returned no overlapping results.

target.title: fix(ui): avoid splitting UTF-16 surrogate pairs in usage filter chip session label
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where the usage-overview active-filter chip for a single unknown session could emit isolated UTF-16 surrogate halves when the session key contains astral characters (e.g., emoji). ## Why This Change Was Made `renderFilterChips` built the single-session chip label with raw `selectedSessionKey.slice(0, 8)`, which can bisect surrogate pairs. The branch now uses the existing `truncateUtf16Safe` helper (already imported in the file) for a safe UTF-16 prefix. ## User Impact The usage overview filter chip remains well-formed when session keys contain non-BMP characters. ## Evidence - Replaced `selectedSessionKey.slice(0, 8)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(selectedSessionKey, 8)` in `ui/src/pages/usage/view-overview.ts`. - Added a regression test in `ui/src/pages/usage/view-overview.test.ts` that places an astral character **across** the eight-code-unit boundary and asserts the exact rendered label. - Focused test passes: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/usage/view-overview.test.ts -t "renderFilterChips"`. - Lint clean: `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs ui/src/pages/usage/view-overview.ts ui/src/pages/usage/view-overview.test.ts`. ## Real behavior proof - **Behavior addressed:** Before the patch, a session key like `"1234567😀890"` reaches code-unit index 8 inside the emoji surrogate pair. Raw `.slice(0, 8)` returns `"1234567\ud83d"` (isolated high surrogate), while the fix renders `"Session: 1234567…"`. - **Real environment tested:** Local checkout of `fix/usage-filter-chip-utf16` at `28edb6aadc`. - **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** ```bash node --import tsx -e 'import { JSDOM } from "jsdom"; const dom = new JSDOM("

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Microsoft Teams users would send mentions, quoted replies, or forwarded messages and the agent would receive incomplete or misleading text. target.title: fix(feishu): retry transient message send failures
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu text, card, image, or file messages could be dropped when `im.message.create` or `im.message.reply` encountered a transient network or server failure. Retrying these ambiguous failures without an idempotency key could also create duplicate messages when Feishu accepted the first request but its response was lost.

## Why This Change Was Made

Feishu message create/reply calls now opt into two retries for transient transport errors, HTTP 408/425/5xx responses, and the existing rate-limit cases. Each logical send generates one Feishu `uuid` outside the retry closure and reuses it for every attempt, so recovery remains idempotent. Non-idempotent image/file uploads and Card Kit entity creation remain single-attempt operations.

## User Impact

Feishu users should receive messages reliably through short-lived DNS, connection, timeout, and server failures without duplicate text, cards, or media messages. Permanent API errors still fail immediately, and upload behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

- Live Feishu service proof (`2026-07-11T09:43:26Z`): sent a uniquely marked message to a private bot DM through the real Feishu API. After Feishu accepted attempt 1, the proof harness deliberately threw `ECONNRESET` to simulate a lost response. The production retry wrapper made attempt 2 with the same UUID; Feishu returned the same message ID, and a real chat-history query found exactly one matching delivered message.

```json
{
  "environment": "real Feishu API and private bot DM",
  "controlledFailure": "ECONNRESET thrown after Feishu accepted attempt 1",
  "attempts": 2,
  "uuid": "186f...7320",
  "firstAcceptedMessageId": "om_x...e2ab",
  "retryMessageId": "om_x...e2ab",
  "sameMessageId": true,
  "chatId": "oc_0...23ce",
  "historyMatchCount": 1,
  "matchingMessageIds": ["om_x...e2ab"],
  "exactlyOneDelivered": true,
  "result": "PASS"
}
```

- Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/send.retry.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/send.reply-fallback.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/send.test.ts`
- Observed after the patch: a transient first `message.create`/`message.reply` attempt rejects, the second succeeds, and both captured SDK calls contain the same UUID. The focused suite passed `5 files / 157 tests`.
- Upload boundary proof: a transient `image.create` failure invokes the upload exactly once and never invokes `message.create`, confirming non-idempotent uploads are not replayed.
- Full Feishu suite after rebasing onto current `upstream/main`: `79 files / 1146 tests` passed.
- Type checks: extension source and extension test tsgo projects passed.
- Static checks: targeted oxfmt, targeted oxlint, and `git diff --check` passed.
- SDK contract: pinned `@larksuiteoapi/node-sdk@1.68.0` declares `data.uuid?: string` for both `im.message.create` and `im.message.reply`.
- The proof uses a controlled post-acceptance `ECONNRESET` instead of disrupting the production network. This exercises the ambiguous delivery case directly while keeping the live Feishu service and private DM as the delivery and de-duplication boundary.

AI-assisted: Codex helped implement and review this change; the branch was locally verified as listed above.

Related: #90804


### Additional Field Evidence

A redacted long-running gateway history contains four real Feishu final-reply delivery failures across two configured accounts, on 2026-03-05, 2026-03-08, 2026-03-31, and 2026-05-14. Each failure ended with:

```text
Client network socket disconnected before secure TLS connection was established
```

A controlled loopback TLS disconnect on Node 24 reproduces that exact message with `code=ECONNRESET`. The production implementation in this PR classifies `ECONNRESET` as transient and retries the same logical `im.message.create` or `im.message.reply` operation with its stable UUID.

Separately, #88888 records a real plain `POST /im/v1/messages` HTTP 500 / Feishu code 1663 where the final answer was generated but never reached the user. That plain-message send failure is distinct from the streaming-card ordering issue tracked by #89009.

Current main and shipped v2026.6.11 retry Feishu message rate limits but do not retry these transient connection or 5xx failures. Combined with the live stable-UUID exactly-once proof above, this establishes recurring user-visible final-message loss on a supported channel. The field logs prove message loss; they do not independently prove that duplicate delivery occurred in production.

## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI mock has limited curated chat state for design QA, so reviewers have to rely on ad hoc sessions when checking empty chat, longer transcripts, markdown rendering, code blocks, tables, warnings, and recoverable error copy.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR adds stable dev/mock-only fixture sessions to the Control UI mock server. The proposed fixtures cover a New session empty state, a coding session, a response-shape showcase, and a markdown showcase without changing production gateway or session APIs.

## User Impact

There is no production user-facing behavior change. Developers and designers can load stable mock chat sessions for future Control UI visual review.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
